predecessors.name: Duchy of Savoy
predecessors.text: the Savoyard mainland and, from the exchange for Sicily, the island of Sardinia

successors.name: Kingdom of Italy
successors.text: the Sardinian state with Lombardy, central Italy, the Two Sicilies, Marche and Umbria, as the kingdom of Italy drew it from 1861

ledger.x: 1721: the Savoyard state continues as the Kingdom of Sardinia.
October 1733: Franco-Sardinian troops enter the Duchy of Milan.
1738: the occupation of Milanese land ends with the peace.
1738: the Treaty of Vienna gives Sardinia Novara and Tortona.
13 September 1743: the Treaty of Worms cedes the Milanese west of the Ticino.
April 1744: Franco-Spanish troops take Villefranche.
September 1745: the Franco-Spanish army takes Alessandria, Valenza and Casale.
18 October 1748: the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the war ('on 18 October 1748, the war ended with the signing of the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle').
18 October 1748: the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the war.
1767-1769: Charles Emmanuel III annexes the Maddalena archipelago.
1792: France annexes Savoy.
29 September 1792: French troops enter Nice.
April 1796: Napoleon's armistice puts French garrisons in three fortress districts.
15 May 1796: the Treaty of Paris turns the occupation of Nice into a cession ('the county of Nice, the duchy of Savoy, Tende and Beuil' to France; next entry).
15 May 1796: the Treaty of Paris cedes Nice to France.
December 1798: the fortress districts of 1796 merge into the occupation of all Piedmont.
December 1798: the court leaves Turin for Cagliari.
December 1798: France occupies Piedmont.
June 1799: Austro-Russian troops end the Piedmontese Republic.
June 1799: the Austrians hold Piedmont.
June 1800: Napoleon retakes Piedmont.
June 1800: France holds Piedmont again, as the Subalpine Republic (1800-1802).
11 September 1802: the Subalpine Republic ends.
11 September 1802: Piedmont and Aosta become French departements.
11 September 1802: the Novarese goes to the Italian Republic.
1814: the court returns from Cagliari to Turin.
1814: Piedmont and Aosta return to the crown.
1814: the crown takes Liguria from Genoa.
30 May 1814: Savoy (except the Annecy-Chambery part) and Nice return to the crown.
1815: the Annecy-Chambery part of Savoy comes back.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 1816: Sardinia gives Carouge to Geneva.
1817: Sardinia takes Monaco under its protection.
Spring 1848: Parma votes to join Sardinia.
23 March 1848: Sardinia declares war on Austria.
8 June 1848: Lombardy votes for annexation.
5 July 1848: Venetia votes for annexation.
9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice gives Lombardy and Venetia back.
9 August 1848: the first campaign ends in the Salasco armistice.
August 1848, after the armistice of Salasco (9 August): Parma goes back to its duke.
20 March 1849: the war resumes.
23 March 1849: Charles Albert is beaten at Novara.
24 March 1849: Austria occupies Lomellina and Alessandria.
6 August 1849: the Treaty of Milan ends the occupation.
26 April 1859: war with Austria over Lombardy.
12 July 1859: the Armistice of Villafranca ends the fighting.
1859: Lombardy joins Sardinia.
22 March 1860: the central Italian provinces are annexed.
24 March 1860: Savoy and Nice go to France.
1860: the Sardinian protectorate over Monaco ends.
11 May 1860: Garibaldi lands at Marsala.
11 September 1860: the invasion of the Papal States.
29 September 1860: Ancona surrenders.
21 October 1860: the Two Sicilies vote to join.
November 1860: Marche and Umbria vote to join.
13 February 1861: Gaeta surrenders.
17 March 1861: the Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed.

wars.name: War of the Polish Succession (Sardinian front)
wars.outcome: Franco-Sardinian troops entered Milanese territory in October 1733 and held Milan from 3 November; the Treaty of Vienna (November 1738) gave Sardinia the lands west of the Ticino including Novara and Tortona.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession (Sardinian front)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Worms, 13 September 1743: Austria cedes the Milanese west of the Ticino and Lake Maggiore to Sardinia; Franco-Spanish troops take Villefranche (April 1744) and, after Bassignano (27 September 1745), Alessandria, Valenza and Casale; Peace of…

wars.name: War of the First Coalition (Sardinian front)
wars.outcome: Savoy annexed by France in 1792; Armistice of Cherasco, 28 April 1796 (Alessandria, Coni, Tortona to France); Treaty of Paris, 15 May 1796: Nice, Savoy, Tende and Beuil ceded and free passage for French troops.

wars.name: First Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Sardinia declared war on 23 March 1848, annexed Lombardy (8 June) and Venetia (5 July), lost at Custoza (25 July), withdrew by the Salasco armistice (9 August 1848), lost at Novara (23 March 1849); Charles Albert abdicated; Treaty of Milan, 6 August 1849…

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: War from 26 April 1859; Magenta 4 June, Solferino 24 June; Armistice of Villafranca 12 July; Treaty of Zurich 11 November: Austria ceded Lombardy to France, which gave it to Sardinia, except Mantua and Legnago.

wars.name: Expedition of the Thousand and the annexation of the south
wars.outcome: Garibaldi landed at Marsala on 11 May 1860 and entered Naples on 7 September; the Piedmontese army invaded the Papal States on 11 September; a plebiscite of 21 October 1860 annexed the Two Sicilies; Gaeta fell on 13 February 1861; the Kingdom of Italy was…

certainty.note: Frontiers fixed by treaty: The Hague (17 February 1720), Vienna (November 1738), Aix-la-Chapelle (18 October 1748).
Annexations, armistice garrisons and client republics (the Piedmontese and Subalpine republics) make the mainland frontier a matter of occupation; the island is sharp.
Frontiers fixed by treaty: Congress of Vienna (1814-15), Carouge to Geneva (1816), Milan (6 August 1849), Zurich (11 November 1859), Turin (24 March 1860).
